missionPremise: Plan row P-318, added by A-210 on 2026-09-17 (90_operations/OPS-16_texas_market_plan_of_record.md line 567): a required check that cannot run blocks its own pull request forever. hauska-map `main` requires the status contexts `test` and `No double-encoded source` with strict=true and enforce_admins=true, but `test` is path-filtered, so a pull request changing a path outside those filters never produces it — and GitHub then refuses the merge with `Required status check "test" is expected.` even for an admin. Measured on the P-305 lane's #410, which changes only `.github/workflows/property-explorer-sync-retrieval-key.yml`. The two available escapes are both worse than the defect: turning enforce_admins off, or pushing an unrelated app-file edit to make CI fire (the second escape is literally recommended in a comment in command-center-ci.yml today). Sources read at source this session: the plan row; the branch protection object; #410's file list and its full check-run set; PR #411's check-run set as the PE-only baseline.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate all of the following without me: (1) a pull request exists whose diff is one workflow file and whose head reports BOTH required contexts, `test` and `No double-encoded source`, each with the literal check-run conclusion `success`, with the run URL for each; (2) the `test` check-run for that pull request is shown to have EXECUTED the suite (named steps, non-zero durations, no `skipped`/`neutral`), not merely to have reported; (3) a control pull request whose diff is one workflow file and which does NOT carry the fix is shown to report only `No double-encoded source` (exactly one check-run) with mergeStateStatus BLOCKED — the miss reproduced on a file other than #410's; (4) a pull request whose diff is only `apps/property-explorer/**` still reports both contexts under the fixed workflow; (5) the close names every file class that can change without producing `test` today and says which of them a required check should cover.
scopeBasis: The build is exactly the dispatch's item 1, in the smallest form the dispatch itself names: add the workflow paths to property-explorer-ci.yml's pull_request.paths. Everything else the dispatch asks for is a REPORT, not a build — item 3 (the uncovered file-class list) and the either-way answer about command-center-ci.yml and factory-console-ci.yml. Deliberately excluded, each with a reason: (a) changing which contexts are required, or any other branch-protection or enforce_admins change — the dispatch reserves that to the operator, and 91_branch_protection_runbook records the reversal criteria that make it a ruling; (b) merging anything; (c) touching #410 or any other lane's branch; (d) adding app-file paths (api/spine.ts, packages/instrument-registry/**, root package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, vercel.json) to the trigger — those are real gaps in the same class, but item 1 scopes the build to workflow files and item 3 scopes the rest to reporting, and widening a trigger changes CI cost on ordinary pull requests, which is the operator's call, not this lane's; (e) rotating or editing any secret, deploy or traffic shift. The 4th falsifier is the dispatch's own; a 5th control was added because the fix CREATES a condition the repo has never had on this path — two check-runs named `test` on one head — and an unmeasured blast radius on a CI control is the defect class this repo keeps finding (DEV_PROCESS 2.4).

threeProducersOneName.claim: Three workflows each define a job whose check-run name is exactly `test`, and the required context is matched by name: property-explorer-ci.yml (job id `test`, explicit name `test`), command-center-ci.yml (job id `test`, no name override), factory-console-ci.yml (job id `test`, explicit name `test`).
threeProducersOneName.method: Read at source from the three workflow files at origin/main 3ee35d5e; the job ids are `test` in all three.
threeProducersOneName.consequence: The required context `test` is co-owned by three workflows and is satisfied by ANY ONE of them succeeding. A green `test` on a given pull request therefore means 'one of three suites passed', not 'the suite passed'. The dispatch's premise states `test` comes from property-explorer-ci.yml; that is true but incomplete, and the incomplete form is what makes the CI workaround comment in command-center-ci.yml look reasonable.

thePrecedent.commit: c379df06ea926f721e23c4b0ba5578cd871d319d, 2026-08-31, 'ci: let .gitattributes trigger the CI it can break'
thePrecedent.shape: The same defect class, fixed the same way: a file that can break every suite was in no trigger's path filter, so a change to it produced no CI at all. Fixed by adding .gitattributes to all three test workflows' path lists — deliberately NOT to the sync-retrieval-key or publish workflows, 'which are deploy and release jobs rather than tests'.
thePrecedent.whyItMattersHere: It is also the origin of the phrase in the plan row: a check that cannot fire on the input most able to break it. And it fixes the precedent for which workflows own the paths.

theChange.edit: In `on.pull_request.paths`, replace the self-reference `- ".github/workflows/property-explorer-ci.yml"` with `- ".github/workflows/**"`, carrying an incident-anchored comment naming P-318, the measured #410 miss, and why the whole directory rather than a list of today's workflows (a NEW workflow file is the same miss by construction). `.gitattributes` and the four app/package paths are untouched.
theChange.whyThisOwner: The dispatch names property-explorer-ci.yml as the smallest form. It is also the right owner on merit: its `test` job is the broadest of the three (it installs the frozen lockfile, builds the shared map-renderer, and runs the parcel-fact-sheet contract suite and the property-explorer suite plus three guards), so it is the most meaningful single suite to run for a change that touches no app path at all.
theChange.whyNotAllThree: The .gitattributes precedent added its path to all three test workflows because a checkout-policy change can break any of the three suites. A change to a workflow file cannot break any of them, and this change only has to make the required context REPORT. Adding the glob to all three would triple the Actions cost of every workflow-only pull request and create three check-runs named `test` on heads that today produce one. The alternative is stated in the close so the operator can rule on it; the dispatch asked for the smallest form and this is it.
theChange.whatWouldMakeMeNotBuild: If `test` from Property Explorer CI turned out NOT to satisfy the required context on a workflow-only diff (i.e. if the requirement were bound to a workflow identity rather than the bare name), falsifier 1 would fail and the honest response would be to build nothing and report that the fix is a required-context change, which is the operator's. The pre-registered likelihood order for that outcome is in falsifiersPreRegisteredForMyOwnRole.

alternativesConsideredAndRejected.makeTestUnfiltered: Remove `paths:` from property-explorer-ci.yml's pull_request trigger so `test` reports on every PR. Rejected as the change to make HERE: it is strictly larger than the dispatch's smallest form, it runs the full PE suite on every docs-only or command-center pull request, and it silently changes CI cost for every other lane. Named in the close as the option that would close the whole class in one edit.
alternativesConsideredAndRejected.changeTheRequiredContexts: Require the three distinct check names (or a single always-on context) instead. Rejected for building: branch protection is the operator's per the dispatch, and 91_branch_protection_runbook makes context changes a ruling with a reliability report behind them. Reported, not built.
alternativesConsideredAndRejected.aDedicatedAlwaysOnWorkflowNamedTest: Rejected outright: a workflow that exists only to report `test` without running a suite is exactly the no-op-satisfies-the-requirement defect class the dispatch's item 2 forbids and 91_branch_protection_runbook names ('skipped counts as passing').
alternativesConsideredAndRejected.fixItInTheFourAppWorkflowsToo: Adding the glob to all three test workflows - see whyNotAllThree.

falsifiersPreRegisteredForMyOwnRole.readingRule: Held BEFORE anything was built or pushed, and stated as an expected outcome so a miss is a finding rather than a fitted result (DEV_PROCESS 4.5). If a falsifier comes out against an expectation, the expectation is what gets reported, not the run.

falsifier1_workflowOnlyDiffProducesBothC.expected: PASS. The deliverable pull request's own head is a workflow-only diff, so its `test` check-run must be `completed :: success` from Property Explorer CI and `No double-encoded source` must be `completed :: success`, and the pull request must stop being BLOCKED by a missing required context.
falsifier1_workflowOnlyDiffProducesBothC.likelihoodOrderIfItFails: (1) `test` reports but GitHub still refuses the merge because the required context is matched to something narrower than the bare check-run name — this would falsify the dispatch's premise and the honest response is to build nothing and recommend a context change; (2) the YAML fails to parse and NO workflow runs at all, which is visible as zero runs rather than a missing one; (3) the `test` job fails on the workflow-only tree for an unrelated pre-existing reason — controlled for by running the same suites locally before pushing.
falsifier1_workflowOnlyDiffProducesBothC.residualRisk: The workflow file is evaluated from the head SHA for pull_request events, so the fixed path list is the one under test. Stated because it is the mechanism the whole fix depends on.

falsifier2_peOnlyDiffStillProduces.expected: PASS. With the fixed workflow in the head and an app-only diff (base = the deliverable branch), Property Explorer CI must trigger and `test` must be `completed :: success`; `No double-encoded source` must also report (it has no path filter, so it cannot regress, but it is asserted rather than assumed).
falsifier2_peOnlyDiffStillProduces.likelihoodOrderIfItFails: (1) the nested base is the reason — a pull request based on a non-default branch reports differently, in which case the isolation method is what failed, not the fix, and I say so and fall back to the ambiguous attribution with that stated as a hole; (2) the edit accidentally removed one of the existing paths — controlled for by diffing the change and showing the removal count.
falsifier2_peOnlyDiffStillProduces.whyNestedBase: GitHub evaluates pull_request.paths against the diff against the pull request's base and runs the workflow version from the head. Basing the control on the deliverable branch is the only way to have the head carry the FIX while the diff stays app-only; based on main the diff would contain the fix and the attribution would be ambiguous (both the workflow path and the app path would match).

falsifier3_revertReproducesTheMiss.expected: PASS (i.e. the miss reproduces). A workflow-only diff against UNFIXED main must produce exactly one check-run — `No double-encoded source` :: success — with no `test` check-run at all, and mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. This is the positive control for falsifier 1: without it, a green `test` on the deliverable is not evidence that the path change is what caused it.
falsifier3_revertReproducesTheMiss.likelihoodOrderIfItFails: (1) GitHub reports `test` anyway from one of the other two co-owners — impossible for publish-map-renderer.yml since it is in neither list, so this would mean a producer I have not found, which would itself be the finding; (2) the diff accidentally includes a second file, which would invalidate the control — checked by reading the pull request's file list before recording the result.
falsifier3_revertReproducesTheMiss.residualRisk: GitHub sometimes reports a required context as 'Expected' rather than absent; the measurement is the check-run set for the head SHA plus mergeStateStatus, both read from the API, never from the pull request page's rendering.

falsifier4_theTestJobReallyExecutes.expected: PASS. On the deliverable's head, the `test` job's steps must each be `completed :: success` with a non-zero duration: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm --filter @empressaio/parcel-fact-sheet test`, `pnpm --filter property-explorer test`, `Records copy guard (P-85 item 16)`, `Retired checkout seam guard (P-103)`, `Public pages guard (P-108)`. A `skipped` or `neutral` conclusion on any step, or a job with an `if:` that can short-circuit it, FAILS this falsifier.
falsifier4_theTestJobReallyExecutes.staticHalf: Read at source before the run: the `test` job in property-explorer-ci.yml carries no `if:`, no `continue-on-error`, and no path-conditional step, so it cannot skip itself — the 91_branch_protection_runbook 'skipped counts as passing' hazard is absent for this job on inspection. The dynamic half is the run's own step conclusions and durations.
falsifier4_theTestJobReallyExecutes.residualRisk: A step that 'runs' but short-circuits internally would still be `success`; the two test commands print their suite counts, so the durations plus the job log are read together rather than trusting the conclusion alone.

falsifier5_added_duplicateNamesAreSafe.whyAdded: The fix creates a condition the repo has not had on this path: a change to command-center-ci.yml will now trigger BOTH Command Center CI and Property Explorer CI, producing two check-runs named `test` on one head. `test` is a required context and the repo has three producers of that name; an unmeasured blast radius on a CI control is the defect class this program hunts (DEV_PROCESS 2.4: paired controls need a divergence test).
falsifier5_added_duplicateNamesAreSafe.expected: PASS with a new observation: exactly two check-runs named `test` (one app github-actions), both `completed :: success`, `No double-encoded source` also success, and the pull request's required contexts satisfied (not BLOCKED for a missing context). Cost stated: a workflow-only change now runs the full Property Explorer suite as well as the workflow's own.
falsifier5_added_duplicateNamesAreSafe.likelihoodOrderIfItFails: (1) GitHub reports `Expected` despite two successes because duplicate names confuse the required-context evaluation — that would mean the fix trades one blocked state for another on command-center-ci.yml changes, and the recommendation changes to unfiltering one workflow; (2) one of the two suites fails on a workflow-only tree for an unrelated reason. Both are reported as findings, and in case (1) the deliverable is NOT withdrawn (it still closes the sync-retrieval-key case, which triggers only the new producer) but the close says so plainly.
falsifier5_added_duplicateNamesAreSafe.residualRisk: This control does not test the mixed case (one producer success, one failure, same name). That case is NOT measured and is stated as a hole, not smoothed over: what a green `test` guarantees when three producers share the name is a question about the required-context design, and the answer belongs with the operator's ruling on the context set.

knownHolesStatedNotDiscovered: The fix relies on a check-run NAME that has three producers. Only one of them must succeed for the required context, so `test` is not a per-suite guarantee and never was. This lane does not change that; it makes the name reachable from one more path. Named for the operator, not fixed.
The mixed duplicate case (two producers, one success and one failure, same name) is not measured by control D and is not claimed.

A workflow-only pull request now runs the full Property Explorer suite. That is the point (a meaningful check rather than a no-op), and it is also a new cost on workflow-only changes; the cost is bounded to that path class.

The negative control's file is publish-map-renderer.yml, not #410's file. The dispatch forbids pushing to #410. The class is identical; the file is deliberately different, and the close says so rather than implying #410 was re-run.

Whether a green `test` on a `.github/workflows/**`-only change proves anything about the OTHER three workflow files' own jobs (e.g. that a factory-console-ci.yml change breaks nothing there) is not measured: the fix only guarantees a required context reports. The uncovered-class report says which classes still have no suite at all.
The stale comment in command-center-ci.yml is reported and not edited; if it is believed by the next lane, that lane takes the workaround path this row exists to retire.
outOfScope: Any branch-protection change, including changing which contexts are required, disabling enforce_admins, or adding contexts.
Merging anything; pushing to #410 (feat/p305-key-drift-check) or any other lane's branch; force-updating main.
Any deploy, traffic shift, secret or environment change.
